task_instance: Given a small self-contained Django-style views.py file (sample_app/views.py, created as the review target) containing a mix of vulnerable and safe patterns (raw SQL string interpolation, shell=True command injection, unsafe yaml.load, path traversal, open redirect, MD5 password hashing, plus a settings-based URL and an ORM query as safe controls), perform a security review following the skill's process: detect context, trace whether each input is attacker-controlled vs server-controlled, and produce a Markdown report of only HIGH-confidence findings in the skill's specified Output Format (Summary, Findings with Location/Confidence/Issue/Impact/Evidence/Fix, Not Flagged, Needs Verification).
evidence: Created /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_div/getsentry__skills__security-review@office-assistant/sample_app/views.py as the review target (8 functions: 6 vulnerable, 2 safe-by-design). Used Grep on that file to locate attacker-controlled-input sink patterns (request.GET/POST, shell=True, yaml.load, hashlib.md5, redirect(, open() ) at lines 18,28-30,36-38,44,47,53,55,78, matching the skill's 'Quick Patterns Reference' and 'Attacker-Controlled vs Server-Controlled' tables. For each hit, traced the data source (request.GET/POST = attacker-controlled per the skill's table) versus the two safe cases (settings.INTERNAL_STATUS_URL = server-controlled config; User.objects.filter(id=...) = ORM-parameterized), per the skill's 'Research Before Flagging' / 'Verify Exploitability' steps. Wrote the final review to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_div/getsentry__skills__security-review@office-assistant/security_review_report.md containing 6 HIGH-confidence findings (SQL injection, OS command injection, insecure YAML deserialization, path traversal, open redirect, weak MD5 password hashing) each with Location/Confidence/Issue/Impact/Evidence/Fix, a 'Not Flagged' section explaining why the two safe patterns were excluded, and an empty 'Needs Verification' section, in the exact Markdown structure the skill's Output Format section specifies. Verified the deliverable by re-reading the report content in-context and cross-checking each finding's line numbers and code snippet against the source file and against the skill's own classification tables (e.g. request.GET is listed as attacker-controlled, settings.X and ORM .filter() as safe). The entire task -- reading the target file, grepping for patterns, reasoning about data flow, and writing a structured Markdown report -- required only text file read/write and pattern search, none of which needed shell execution, code execution, binary output, or any connector/MCP tool, so no blocker was encountered.
